extracted.intended_audience: State and local education agency administrators, grant writers, and education policymakers (SEAs/LEAs)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference guide describing allocation formulas, eligibility rules, allowable uses, set‑asides, state/LEA responsibilities, and priorities for Federal K–12 grant programs under ESSA. Intended to guide SEAs/LEAs and grant applicants in applying for and administering ESSA funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formula children as basis for Title I, Part A allocations
rubrics_metrics.description: All four Title I, Part A formulas are based on the number of “formula children” (primarily children from low-income families) and factors such as the LEA’s poverty rate and State per‑pupil expenditures; the final Federal‑State allocation produces a single Title I, Part A award to each qualifying LEA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Children counted for allocation purposes include low‑income children, children in families receiving TANF, children in foster homes, and children in local institutions for neglected and delinquent children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title I, Part A Basic Grant eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic Grants are awarded to school districts with at least 10 formula children who make up more than 2 percent of their school‑age population (children ages 5 to 17).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An LEA must meet the numeric and percentage thresholds (≥10 formula children and >2% of school‑age population) to qualify for a Basic Grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title I, Part A Concentration Grant eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Concentration Grants provide additional funds to LEAs in which the number of formula children exceeds 6,500 or 15 percent of the total school‑age population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concentration Grants supplement LEAs serving very large numbers or high percentages of formula children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title I, Part A Targeted Grant eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Targeted Grants weight child counts to make higher payments to LEAs with high numbers/percentages of formula students; to be eligible an LEA must have at least 10 formula children and the count of formula children must equal at least 5 percent of the school‑age population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targeted Grants concentrate resources where proportions of formula children meet the threshold (≥5%) and numeric minimum (≥10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Within‑district Title I allocations and school poverty service ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: LEAs generally use poverty data (e.g., free/reduced‑price lunch eligibility) to allocate Title I funds to schools; LEAs with >1,000 students must serve, in rank order by poverty rate, all schools with poverty rates above 75% (including middle/high schools) before serving lower‑poverty schools. Under ESSA an LEA may lower the high‑school threshold from 75% to 50%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LEAs must rank schools by poverty and follow the statutory order unless lowering the high‑school threshold as allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: State reservations and administrative/direct student services under Title I, Part A
rubrics_metrics.description: States may reserve up to 1 percent (or $400,000, whichever is greater) for State administration of Title I programs, and may reserve up to 3 percent to make grants to LEAs to carry out direct student services (of which the SEA may use not more than 1 percent to administer that program).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State reservations reduce LEA awards; reservation caps and the administrative sublimits must be observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title I, Part A School Improvement reservation
rubrics_metrics.description: States must reserve the greater of 7 percent of combined Title I, Part A allocations to LEAs or the sum of their FY2016 reservation under prior terms (max 4%) plus FY2016 SIG allocation; the SEA must allocate at least 95 percent of its reservation for grants to LEAs on a formula or competitive basis to schools implementing comprehensive or targeted support and improvement activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At least 95% of the reservation must be awarded to LEAs (formula or competitive) for school improvement; remaining reservation uses are limited by statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title I, Part B State Assessments formula and minimum allotments
rubrics_metrics.description: After reservation for assessment system audits, the Secretary must allocate remaining amounts by formula to States; each State receives $3 million assuming sufficient funds, otherwise ratable reductions apply; remaining funds are allocated proportionately according to each State’s relative share of students aged 5–17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appropriations are insufficient to meet the $3 million floor for every State the amounts are ratably reduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment System Audits reserve and grants
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary must reserve up to 20 percent of the appropriation for grants to States for assessment system audits; the minimum grant amount is $1.5 million. For States not applying, funds are reallocated proportionately according to relative share of students aged 5–17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States seeking Audit funds must apply; nonapplicants' shares are redistributed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive grants and excess funds for State Assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: If appropriations exceed a trigger amount, excess funds must be used for competitive grants to SEAs or consortia; grants must be proportional to number of students aged 5–17 in the State(s). Remaining funds after competitive awards are allotted to States or consortia that did not receive a grant in proportion to their student shares.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competitive awards are distributed to reflect proportional student counts; leftover funds revert to proportional State allotments.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Assessments deferral contingent on appropriations (trigger amount)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Congress appropriates less than the trigger amount ($369.1 million) for State Assessments, States may defer commencement or administration of State assessments—their compliance is contingent on the appropriation level for the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriation levels determine whether assessment requirements can be enforced or deferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: State reserve for subgrants under Assessment System Audits
rubrics_metrics.description: Each State must reserve not less than 20 percent of grant funds awarded under Assessment System Audits to make subgrants to LEAs or consortia of LEAs based on demonstrated need in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A minimum 20% set‑aside for LEA subgrants is required; subgrants are need‑based according to applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Migrant Education eligible children definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible migratory children are children of migratory agricultural workers or fishers (or who are themselves migratory workers/fishers) who made a 'qualifying move' within the last 3 years: a residence change due to economic necessity that crosses school district boundaries, is to obtain/resulted in temporary or seasonal agricultural/fishing work, and occurred in the preceding 36 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must identify qualifying moves and count eligible migratory children for allocation purposes (averaged over preceding 3 years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Migrant Education State grant formula and hold‑harmless
rubrics_metrics.description: State grants are based on the average number of identified eligible migratory children (aged 3–21) residing in the State over the prior 3 years and children who received services in summer/intersession programs; under a hold‑harmless provision States are assured of at least 90% of prior years’ allocations for FY2017–2019.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculations use a 3‑year average and service counts; hold‑harmless protects State funding during transitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Migrant Education coordination and consortium incentive grants
rubrics_metrics.description: ED may set aside up to $10 million for contracts/grants to improve inter‑ and intra‑State migrant coordination (including credit accrual/exchange) and may reserve up to $3 million to award consortium incentive grants (competitive grants up to $250,000) to SEAs that propose consortium arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserved funds support coordination and encourage interstate consortia; grants limited to 5 years for coordination awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neglected and Delinquent (Title I, Part D) allocation basis
rubrics_metrics.description: State allocations are based on the number of neglected or delinquent children and youth in State‑run institutions, community day programs, and adult correctional facilities who meet specified enrollment hours thresholds (≥15 hours/week in adult corrections or ≥20 hours/week in institutions/community day programs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only children meeting minimum weekly educational hours are counted for allocation purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neglected and Delinquent State reservation for Transition Services
rubrics_metrics.description: States are required to reserve between 15 and 30 percent of their allocations for projects to help neglected and delinquent participants transition from State institutions to locally operated programs or support successful entry into postsecondary and CTE programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A statutory 15–30% reservation must be used for transition‑focused projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting Effective Instruction State Grants (Title II, Part A) base allocation/hold harmless
rubrics_metrics.description: Each State receives an amount equal to what it received for FY2001 under prior programs (Eisenhower PD and Class Size Reduction); beginning 2017–2022 the base allocation/hold harmless is reduced each fiscal year by 14.29% multiplied by the number of years removed from 2016 (phase‑out).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must account for the hold‑harmless baseline and statutory phase‑out schedule when calculating allocations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title II, Part A State administrative and subgrant requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: States may use up to 1 percent for administrative costs, reserve remaining funds for State‑level activities, and must reserve at least 95 percent for subgrants to LEAs; of the subgrant reserved amount, States may reserve up to 3 percent for State activities aimed at improving principals and school leaders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At least 95% of the State award must be subgranted to LEAs; State administrative and leadership set‑asides are capped.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title II, Part A LEA allocation formula
rubrics_metrics.description: If appropriation is sufficient to meet base allocations, remaining funds are allocated according to a formula that considers population (ages 5–17) and poverty (ages 5–17), with the exception that no State may receive less than 0.5 percent of remaining funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LEA allocations under State subgrant formula are based on each LEA’s share of children aged 5–17 and of children from low‑income families.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder engagement requirement for Title II, Part A use of funds
rubrics_metrics.description: LEAs must consult with teachers, principals, and other stakeholders in determining best uses of Title II, Part A funds; States may require LEAs to confirm stakeholder involvement in their applications, including how funds will likely positively impact student achievement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation or confirmation of stakeholder consultation may be required in LEA applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language Acquisition (Title III) State and LEA subgrant rules
rubrics_metrics.description: ED uses 92.5% of funds for formula grants to States (80% weighted by ELs, 20% by recent immigrants); States must use at least 95% for subgrants to LEAs (subgrants must be >$10,000), and LEAs may use not more than 2% of such funds for administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subgrants must be based primarily on each subgrantee’s share of ELs and require an LEA plan describing assistance to ELs tied to State assessment and long‑term goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title III supplemental funds for surges in immigrant students
rubrics_metrics.description: States must provide additional funding to subgrantees that have experienced a significant increase in percentage or number of recent immigrant students over the preceding 2 years, and may use up to 15 percent of awards for this purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental surge funds are carved out of subgrant allocations to respond to rapid immigrant student increases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title III data counts and allowable sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary may use American Community Survey (ACS) data, State‑provided data, or a combination to determine counts of English learners and immigrant students; ESSA authorizes combining ACS and State data for EL counts and continuing ACS for immigrant counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States should be prepared to document and reconcile ACS and State counts per ED guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title III State‑level activities cap and administrative sublimit
rubrics_metrics.description: States may use up to 5 percent of their allocation for State‑level activities (professional development, planning, evaluation, technical assistance); State planning and direct administrative costs may not exceed 50 percent of the State set‑aside or $175,000, whichever is greater.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The State set‑aside for activities is capped and an upper bound on admin/planning costs applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Support and Academic Enrichment Grants (Title IV, Part A) LEA needs assessment threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: LEAs receiving $30,000 or more must conduct a comprehensive needs assessment and, based on results, use funds according to statutory set‑asides and priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The comprehensive needs assessment determines allocation across required spending areas and priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IV, Part A statutory set‑asides for LEAs receiving ≥$30,000
rubrics_metrics.description: LEAs receiving $30,000 or more must use not less than 20 percent to support well‑rounded educational opportunities, not less than 20 percent to support safe and healthy students, and allocate a portion to support the effective use of technology (with a cap that not more than 15 percent of the allocation may be used to purchase technology infrastructure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LEAs must comply with the 20/20 minimums and the 15% cap on technology infrastructure purchases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IV, Part A minimum LEA award and LEA use rules for smaller allocations
rubrics_metrics.description: No LEA may receive less than $10,000; LEAs receiving less than $30,000 must use funds to carry out activities in at least one of the three authorized areas (well‑rounded education, safe and healthy students, effective use of technology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Smaller LEAs have simpler obligations (choose at least one authorized area).

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IV, Part A State administrative and subgrant percentages
rubrics_metrics.description: ED reserves 0.5% for Outlying Areas, 0.5% for BIE, and 2% for technical assistance; States must use not more than 1 percent for administrative costs and must use not less than 95 percent of their grant award for allocations to LEAs using the Title I, Part A formula.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State administrative caps and minimum subgrant percentages mirror Title I formula distribution conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IV competitive grant award rules and priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: States must award at least 93 percent of certain funds competitively to eligible entities; awards must be at least $50,000 per year for 3–5 year periods. States may require matching (including in‑kind) but match cannot exceed the subgrant amount nor be derived from other Federal or State funds. Priority is given to applications that (1) target students in schools implementing comprehensive or targeted support under Title I; (2) are submitted jointly by at least one Title I LEA and another eligible entity; and (3) demonstrate activities are otherwise inaccessible or expand access to high‑quality services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competitive awards have minimum sizes, terms, allowable matching, and explicit priority criteria that must be documented in applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritization of LEA funds under Title IV (targeting)
rubrics_metrics.description: LEAs must prioritize support to schools with the greatest needs, highest concentrations of educationally disadvantaged children, schools identified for comprehensive or targeted support and improvement under Title I, and schools identified as persistently dangerous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LEAs should document how subgrant uses prioritize these categories when distributing funds to schools.

rubrics_metrics.name: 21st Century Community Learning Centers allowable uses and program hour requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds may be used to provide activities that complement and reinforce the regular school‑day and may fund expanded learning time programs providing students at least 300 additional program hours before, during, or after the traditional school day. Funds may support a broad range of activities to improve academic outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs must align with the regular school day and meet the 300‑hour expanded learning time definition when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: REAP SRSA initial allocation and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: For Small, Rural School Achievement (SRSA) initial allocation: $20,000 plus $100 for each child in average daily attendance (ADA) above 50, with a maximum initial allocation of $60,000. Eligible LEAs must have total ADA <600 or serve only schools in counties with population density <10 persons/sq mile and NCES locale code 41/42/43 or state‑defined rural areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial allocation calculation and eligibility depend on ADA, population density, and NCES locale codes; final allocation is initial allocation minus 'applicable funding' received under certain other programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: REAP‑Flex authority for eligible LEAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible LEAs may consolidate (REAP‑Flex) funds they receive from specified sources (except Title I, Part A) to carry out effective activities under any authorized program, including Title I, Part A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: REAP‑Flex allows fund consolidation for flexibility, but Title I, Part A funds are excluded from consolidation.

rubrics_metrics.name: RLIS eligibility, allocation options, and uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Rural and Low‑Income Schools (RLIS) eligibility requires Census child‑poverty rate ≥20% and serving schools with NCES locale codes 32/33/41/42/43. States may allocate funds to eligible LEAs competitively, via a formula based on ADA in eligible LEAs, or via an alternative formula if it better targets high concentrations of poor students. LEAs may use funds for activities authorized under Parts A of Titles I, II, III, IV and IV Part B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States choose among three allocation options to better target resources to high‑need rural LEAs; program uses mirror other core ESSA program activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indian Education (Title VI) eligibility and minimum allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible entities include LEAs or BIE schools, Indian tribes/organizations, or Indian community‑based organizations; eligibility thresholds are based on number or percent of American Indian/Alaska Native children in an LEA (with exemptions for certain LEAs/areas). Minimum LEA allocation is $3,000. Formula allocation uses APPE in the LEA’s State or 80% of US APPE; ratable reductions apply if insufficient appropriations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may form consortia; calculations follow APPE‑based formulas and observe the $3,000 minimum and ratable reductions when appropriations are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indian Education application and comprehensive plan requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each applicant must annually develop and submit a comprehensive plan for meeting the needs of Indian children, developed in collaboration with a local committee primarily composed of parents and family members. The plan must include student performance goals, explanation of assessment and reporting on progress, and description of proposed professional development activities. Before submitting to the Secretary, an LEA must submit the application to the SEA for comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan is required annually, must be collaborative with parents, and include measurable goals and reporting/PD descriptions; SEA comment precedes Federal submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education for Homeless Children & Youth (McKinney‑Vento/Title IX) State formula and State use of funds
rubrics_metrics.description: After national set‑asides, ED allocates remaining funds to States by a formula based on each State’s share under Title I, Part A, with a State not receiving less than $150,000, 0.25% of total, or FY2001 allocation (whichever is greatest). States may reserve up to 25% (or 50% if receiving the minimum award) for State‑level activities and must distribute remaining funds to LEAs; State awards subgrants to LEAs competitively for terms not to exceed 3 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State reserves and subgrant competition rules determine how funds flow to LEAs; minimum State award thresholds apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local uses of Homeless Education subgrant funds
rubrics_metrics.description: LEAs may use subgrant funds for enriched supplemental instruction, transportation, professional development, referrals to health care, and other services to facilitate enrollment, attendance, and success in school of homeless children, including preschool‑aged children and youth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funds are intended to remove barriers to education for homeless students and may fund a range of supports tied to enrollment/attendance/success.

rubrics_metrics.name: ED national reservations and small set‑aside percentages
rubrics_metrics.description: For many programs ED reserves small percentages for national activities or for the Bureau of Indian Education/Outlying Areas (examples: 0.1% for Outlying Areas, 1% for BIE in some programs; Title I national reservations such as 0.7% for BIE, 0.4% for Outlying Areas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State and LEA allocations are computed after ED makes statutory national reservations; program guidance specifies exact reservation percentages per program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable uses of funds (general program‑specific lists)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each program enumerates permissible activities (examples across programs include professional development, technical assistance, expanded learning time, tutoring aligned to State standards, STEM programs, arts education, college/career counseling, technology infrastructure/PD, transition services, transportation, credit accrual/exchange for migratory students, re‑licensing/reforming certification systems, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and administrators must align proposed activities with the statutory list of allowable uses for the specific program being applied to; some activities have additional statutory caps or priority rules (e.g., tech infrastructure cap in Title IV).
